methodHandling.otherMethods: Not checked; any method behaves like GET.

responses.bodyShape: upstream bytes verbatim (a .pptx zip, starts with 'PK'); content-type forced regardless of upstream type; no cache-control

errors.when: upstream non-2xx (unknown job, job not done, reaped after 24h -> upstream 404)

quirks: Error text differs from pptx-status: 'PPTX service unavailable' here vs 'PPTX service error' there (pptx-result.ts:18 vs pptx-status.ts:17).
Content-type and filename are hard-coded; an upstream HTML/JSON 200 body would be served as a .pptx (Connector guards with a PK magic check).
Body buffered fully (res.arrayBuffer) - no streaming; no size limit.
Repeatable: the same job's result can be re-downloaded until upstream reaps it (Connector comment forge.py:65).
No ownership check; also used for /api/image-to-slide jobs.
beforeAnyState: Unknown jobId or job still running -> 502 {"error":"PPTX service unavailable"}.

callers.expects: res.ok -> blob; else Error('Download failed'). Filename chosen client-side.

Streams with follow_redirects=False (forge.py:937-968) - Darwin follows upstream redirects itself so the Connector sees a 200. Body must start with b'PK' (forge.py:872) and be non-empty; >=400 -> error (confirm: 5xx/429 -> running, other 4xx -> terminal).

docs.openapi: public/openapi.yaml:1056-1075 - matches 200 content-type and disposition. No error responses documented.

planSection65: Row '/api/pptx-result (GET ?jobId=) | pptx bytes' - accurate. Add exact content-type, content-disposition 'attachment; filename="slide.pptx"', 400 'Missing jobId', 502 'PPTX service unavailable'.
